nodes.label: Single-context repo convention
nodes.rationale: This repo is single-context (one control system: Control UI, Pi API, Server API), so domain docs live at the repo root rather than per-subsystem.

nodes.label: /domain-modeling skill
nodes.rationale: Creates CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved, rather than requiring them to exist upfront.

nodes.label: Glossary vocabulary discipline
nodes.rationale: Use terms as defined in CONTEXT.md; don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids. A missing concept is a signal to reconsider invented language or note a real gap.

nodes.label: ADR conflict flagging practice
nodes.rationale: If output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding it.

nodes.label: "Highest available seam" testing philosophy
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure code's checks run through the tool's own execution engine or a real adjacent tool, not mocks -- no pytest/dry-run seam applies to a pyinfra deploy function, so the only faithful check is actually running it.

nodes.label: git_systemd_service live demo (ticket 04)
nodes.rationale: Demoed against a throwaway app/unit before either real Control API Deploy file adopted it: first run applies, second run is fully idempotent (zero pending ops), a code-only change correctly triggers a restart via restarted=code_changed or unit.will_change.

nodes.label: .will_change vs .did_change() distinction
nodes.rationale: did_change() raises if read before the operation executes; .will_change is the property safe to read immediately after calling an operation during the prepare-phase diff -- confirmed by reading OperationMeta in installed pyinfra==3.9.2 and by the demo running without the RuntimeError .did_change() would raise.

nodes.label: Caddyfile.j2 validated with real caddy binary (ticket 07)
nodes.rationale: Rendered templates/Caddyfile.j2 with representative values and ran caddy validate against a real stock caddy binary; wake_on_lan-dependent lines were the only ones that failed on a stock binary, confirming every directive the ticket added is genuinely valid Caddyfile syntax.
nodes.norm_label: caddyfile.j2 validated with real caddy binary (ticket 07)

nodes.label: wake_plugin validated live, caddy-wol retired
nodes.rationale: Built a real Caddy binary with the in-repo wake_plugin module, ran caddy validate against templates/Caddyfile.j2, and ran a live caddy run smoke test against a fake Control Pi API and unreachable upstream -- matching the fail-open, throttled design in .scratch/caddy-wake-plugin/spec.md.

nodes.label: handle_errors-inside-handle_path bug found & fixed
nodes.rationale: Caddy rejects handle_errors nested inside handle_path as "not an ordered HTTP handler"; fixed by moving handle_errors to the site's top level, matched against orig_uri so it still only fires for /server*. Pre-existing bug, independent of caddy-wol vs call_wake_api, surfaced during ADR-0012 revalidation.

nodes.label: @docker connector
nodes.rationale: Image-mode containers start with tail -f /dev/null as PID 1 -- no init system, so systemd.service operations cannot succeed against them out of the box; not documented in prose, derived from reading pyinfra source.

nodes.label: Five-role triage label vocabulary
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix -- recorded as a Status: line since this repo's tracker is local markdown, not GitHub Issues.

nodes.label: Three-tier testing philosophy (--dry, disposable containers, idempotency)
nodes.rationale: No pytest/mypy seam applies to infrastructure code, so checks run through pyinfra's own execution engine: Tier 1 --dry (prepare-phase estimate), Tier 2 disposable systemd-capable containers over @ssh (not @docker, which has no init system), Tier 3 running the same Deploy twice to confirm zero pending operations on the second run.
nodes.norm_label: three-tier testing philosophy (--dry, disposable containers, idempotency)

nodes.label: Typed pydantic-settings config pattern
nodes.rationale: Real addresses/secrets/refs are read from the dev machine's environment at Deploy time via typed pydantic-settings classes rather than each Deploy file parsing os.environ by hand; required settings are constructed lazily inside has_device_role guards so running one Deploy file in isolation never demands env vars an unrelated one needs.

nodes.label: Throttling (~1 call per 10 minutes per URL)
nodes.rationale: Matches caddy-wol's prior per-host throttling behavior.
nodes.norm_label: throttling (~1 call per 10 minutes per url)

nodes.label: xcaddy build with local module override
nodes.rationale: The =./services/... local override is required until this repo is fetchable as a public Go module -- without it xcaddy would try to go get the module path from its VCS host.
nodes.norm_label: xcaddy build with local module override

nodes.label: Verification performed (go test, caddy validate/run)
nodes.rationale: go test covers throttling, different-URL isolation, and fail-open behavior against an httptest.Server; caddy validate and a live caddy run confirm wake-on-error and throttling in a real proxy chain.

nodes.label: ReachabilityTracker (app.py)
nodes.rationale: Logs reachability_changed to Alloy only once per process, since a process can't witness going un-reachable -- it's asleep while that's true.

nodes.label: auth.py (require_tailnet_identity, get_caller_identity)
nodes.rationale: Per ADR-0004, presence of the Tailscale-User-Login header is the entire authorization check -- no allow-list of specific identities.

nodes.label: bind_safety.py (assert_tailnet_only_bind, BindOffTailnetError)
nodes.rationale: A structural backstop for the 'never reachable off-tailnet' requirement, independent of whatever fronts the app.

nodes.label: alloy.py (AlloyLogger.send_event)
nodes.rationale: Both the Pi API and Server API are stateless, so Alloy is the only place wake/suspend/reachability history lives; transport failures are logged and swallowed so a logging outage never blocks the caller's actual action.
